have seen significant upticks, Bank of America said.

According to the firm's August Equity Strategy data, the relative weighting for the semiconductor industry was 1.15x, ahead of software (0.92x) and IT (0.99x). That's up from 1.08x in May and near the peak in the post-ChatGPT era of 1.18x, hit in April 2023, analyst Vivek Arya wrote in a note to clients.
While Nvidia and Broadcom have the broadest ownership in the S&P 500 (followed by AMD at 51%), not all semiconductor stocks are created equal. Skyworks Solutions
is the least owned chip stock at 3%, followed by Microchip
Fund managers are the most overweight in names such as Ciena
, while Skyworks, On Semi, Microchip, and Qualcomm

Additionally, Arya found that ownership has become concentrated in the compute, memory, and semiconductor equipment areas, at 74%, 43%, and 40%, respectively. Memory saw the greatest ownership increase from July, up 612 basis points, while semiconductor equipment rose 324 basis points. The consumer space fell 121 basis points month-over-month.

“Memory still surging, AMD tops 50%, Analog/EDA cool On single stocks, MU’s ownership +608bps MoM to 50%, now the 4th most owned semi, and NVDA ownership rose to 82% as AMD increased to 51% (relative weight +7% MoM/+75% QoQ),” Arya explained. “SNDK ownership jumped +897 bps MoM (largest single increase) to 24%. Analog sector relative weight -4% MoM, EDA -5% MoM. INTC kept rising (ownership +205 bps MoM to 21%) yet remains only the 19th most-owned despite 5th-largest market cap. NVDA/AVGO were the only semis among the most widely sold names funding the SpaceX IPO ($4.4bn/$2.7bn, 44 funds each), though ~1.2% short interest on both likely points to long de-grossing with SPCX now owned by ~53% of funds.”
Other notable findings from the data include that hedge funds prefer Seagate Technology
, and Qualcomm have higher weighting with long-only investors compared to hedge funds.
